# Story 25 — WhatsApp and SMS on one provider gateway (Story: 522)

## Prerequisites

- **Story 24 (Story 7.1 — channel-agnostic intake pipeline) completed.** This plan assumes 7.1 has landed the `Channels` module with a `channel_accounts` table, an inbound routing pipeline that owns idempotency / identification / correlation / quarantine / department resolution, and a `ChannelTransport` port (or the shape that will be widened here). Cross-check the plan for 7.1 in `.squad/plans/inti/24-story-522-521.md` (or the equivalent file the executor for 521 produced) before starting.
- Coordinate with the owner of the Story 4.4 delivery-state pipeline (`backend/app/Modules/Tickets/Domain/Enum/DeliveryState.php` lines 14–23) — this story extends that enum.
- Coordinate with the owner of the Customers module for the phone/WhatsApp identifier work (`backend/app/Modules/Customers/Domain/ContactKind.php` line 7).

---

## Story Goal

Deliver WhatsApp and SMS as two configurations of one provider-gateway implementation on top of the Story 7.1 pipeline. The outcome is:

1. Administrators can register a WhatsApp business number and an SMS number as rows in `channel_accounts`, each with provider, credentials (write-only, encrypted, never returned) and active state.
2. Inbound WhatsApp / SMS messages traverse the exact 7.1 pipeline — no new correlation rule, no new ticket type, no new inbox, no new table.
3. Agents reply on the channel the ticket arrived on through a queued send job with a bounded retry-with-backoff, and delivery state is recorded per message; failed sends remain visible in the timeline with Retry and Edit (UX-09).
4. A **null adapter** ships for both channels so CI passes with no provider reachable.
5. Business-initiated messaging windows (WhatsApp 24-hour session) are surfaced on the composer before the agent writes, using the same treatment as a disabled channel.

**Not in scope.** No template library / approval state / template manager. No general webhook framework (FR-128 stays deferred; each provider gets one signed route only). No per-channel SLA pinning. No escalation-rule table. No organisation chip.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** Inbound is only email; `TicketChannel` has no `Whatsapp` / `Sms`; `DeliveryState` reports only `Queued|Sent|Failed`; identifiers are `Email|Phone`; there is no `ChannelTransport` port for non-email channels.
- **New behaviour:** WhatsApp and SMS are configured as `channel_accounts` rows; inbound flows through the Story 7.1 pipeline unchanged; a single `ChannelTransport` port has two adapters per channel (real + null); the send job is one job with bounded retry; delivery state extends only with states the providers actually report; the `Whatsapp` contact kind is separate from `Phone`; a WhatsApp 24-hour window disables composing with the same treatment as a disabled channel.

### 4 — Outbound send job (one job, one retry policy)

- **Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Channels/Jobs/SendOutboundChannelMessageJob.php`** — model on `backend/app/Modules/Email/Jobs/SendOutboundEmailJob.php`. Shape:
  - Explicit `timeout` and `tries`; backoff array (e.g. `[10, 30, 90]`).
  - Resolve the `ChannelTransport` bound for the message's channel via the service provider.
  - On success: set `messages.delivery_state = Accepted` (or `Sent` — align with 7.1's semantics), capture provider message id.
  - On `ChannelTransportFailure::temporary()`: rethrow so the queue retries within the backoff schedule.
  - On `ChannelTransportFailure::permanent()`: transition `delivery_state = Undeliverable` (or `Failed` when the provider distinguishes the two), record the reason on the message row without leaking credentials.
- **The job is shared by WhatsApp and SMS.** No channel-specific job class exists anywhere.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Same digits used for `Phone` and `Whatsapp`.** Inbound resolution must match on `(kind, value)`, then fall back to a phone match. The customer record stores both rows; no merge, no dedupe. Enforced in the resolver extended in Backend §7.
- **WhatsApp 24-hour session closed.** Composer disables with the same treatment as a disabled channel, reason surfaced from `OutboundEligibility` (Backend §6) before the agent writes. Never let the send job be queued in this state.
- **Provider unreachable.** Send job raises `ChannelTransportFailure::temporary()`, retries per policy, then transitions to `Failed`. Ticket creation, assignment, escalation, reply, resolve continue unaffected. UI shows the failure with Retry / Edit; queue keeps working.
- **Provider signature mismatch on webhook.** Controller returns `401` **before** reading the body. Never log the raw payload on signature failure; log only the fact and the source IP (redact everything else).
- **Provider reports a state we do not model.** Log a structured warning; do not invent a delivery state. The message stays in its last valid state.
- **Credential in a log line or exception message.** All adapters must strip credentials before rethrowing. Audit-redactor entry from Backend §8 catches audit-writer paths. Regression covered by `CredentialsNeverLeakTest` sibling test (see Test Plan).
- **Null adapter in CI.** With no provider configured, `SendOutboundChannelMessageJob` runs against `NullChannelTransport` and marks the message `Accepted`. The full suite must pass under this configuration.
- **Adapter swap.** Replacing WhatsApp Cloud API with a hypothetical second WhatsApp provider must produce the same ticket, the same correlation, the same history rows for the same inbound payload. Enforced by `TwoAdaptersSamePayloadTest`.
- **Outbound on an inactive channel account.** Blocked at `OutboundEligibility`; the send job is never enqueued. The API returns a Problem-Details refusal with the reason string, not a 500.
- **Unicode / RTL in a message body.** Message body is stored verbatim; the composer already handles RTL — no channel-specific handling.
- **Duplicate webhook delivery.** The Story 7.1 idempotency key on `(channel, provider_message_id)` (see `.squad/stories/inti/521/intake.md` line 23) already dedupes — this story adds nothing new.

## Migration / Rollback

- **No new tables.** Changes are:
  - Alter `ticket_channel` enum (via a migration that widens the enum's allowed values — check-constraint on Postgres, string column on SQLite).
  - Alter `messages.delivery_state` enum similarly.
  - Alter `contact_identifiers.kind` enum similarly.
  - Add `whatsapp` value support and any `channel_accounts` column adjustments (e.g. `provider` string) — piggyback on the 7.1 table; do not create a parallel one.
- Migrations live under `backend/app/Modules/Channels/Database/Migrations/` (folder created in 7.1) with the `2026_09_..._add_whatsapp_and_sms_to_channel_enums.php` naming pattern from `backend/app/Modules/Tickets/Database/Migrations/2026_09_15_000100_allow_internal_message_direction.php`.
- **Rollback.** Each `down()` narrows the enum back to its prior set of values. Because no rows exist for the new values on a rollback path (the feature was never in production), the narrow is safe. If a rollback happens after data has been written, refuse to rollback rather than truncate — mirror the `2026_09_06_000200_drop_reopened_status.php` migration's guard.
- **Half-applied state.** If the enum migration lands but the code does not, existing writes are unaffected (email / portal / agent / system continue to work). If the code lands before the enum, inserting a `whatsapp` value would fail at the database check-constraint — deploy enum first.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** in `backend/`, run `composer install` if needed, then `php artisan migrate --pretend` to confirm the enum widening migration is generated; then `php artisan migrate` on a dev database.
2. **Backend tests:** in `backend/`, run `php artisan test --filter=Channels` and `php artisan test --testsuite=Architecture`. The full suite (`php artisan test`) must pass with **no provider configured** — the null adapters cover both channels.
3. **Backend openapi:** in `backend/`, run `php artisan openapi:generate` then `php artisan openapi:check` to confirm the resource additions land in `backend/openapi.yaml`.
4. **Frontend runs:** in `frontend/`, run `pnpm install` if needed, then `pnpm test` for the vitest suite and `pnpm lint`. Run `pnpm dev` and manually verify (a) the Channels admin section renders WhatsApp / SMS rows and credentials show `configured` after save, (b) the composer disables with reason on an inactive WhatsApp account, (c) a failed send row exposes Retry and Edit.
5. **Regression:** re-run the Story 7.1 integration tests (`php artisan test --filter=Inbound` and the pipeline-level tests) to confirm this story does not change the 7.1 pipeline surface for the email channel.
6. **Regression:** re-run `frontend/__tests__/messages-parity.test.ts` and `frontend/__tests__/a11y/admin.test.tsx` after adding the new admin rows.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `TicketChannel` enum widened to include `Whatsapp` and `Sms` with a migration that widens the DB constraint.
- [ ] `DeliveryState` enum extended with `Accepted`, `Delivered`, `Read`, `Undeliverable`; no invented states.
- [ ] `ContactKind` enum extended with `Whatsapp`; `Phone` and `Whatsapp` are separate identifiers that may hold identical digits.
- [ ] Phone / WhatsApp identifiers are E.164-normalised on both inbound and outbound boundaries.
- [ ] A `ChannelTransport` port exists with real adapters for WhatsApp (Meta Cloud API) and SMS (Twilio) and a `NullChannelTransport` shared default.
- [ ] One `SendOutboundChannelMessageJob` handles both channels with an explicit timeout and bounded retry-with-backoff.
- [ ] Two signed inbound routes exist (`/api/webhooks/channels/whatsapp/{account}` and `/api/webhooks/channels/sms/{account}`); each verifies the provider signature **before** reading the body. No general webhook framework is introduced.
- [ ] Inbound WhatsApp and SMS traverse the Story 7.1 pipeline unchanged (same idempotency, identification, correlation, quarantine, department resolution). No new table.
- [ ] Failed sends stay visible in the timeline with Retry and Edit (UX-09).
- [ ] Credentials are write-only, encrypted at rest, never logged, never returned. Admin UI shows `configured` with no reveal control (UX-16).
- [ ] Composer blocks outbound on inactive channels and on WhatsApp when the 24-hour window is closed, showing the reason before the agent writes.
- [ ] Full test suite passes in CI with no provider reachable (null adapters).
- [ ] `TwoAdaptersSamePayloadTest` proves the adapter is a configuration choice.
- [ ] Architecture tests forbid channel-specific ticket paths outside the enum values.
